a5318d0404da.title: Doctor evidence file is absent from main

cda65fc717ba.title: Publish gate accepts malformed non-block verdicts
cda65fc717ba.observation: decide() blocks only when verdict.verdict is exactly 'block' or when a publish verdict has score=None. A malformed verdict such as verdict='error' with a numeric score, or an unknown verdict token with a score, is treated as SHIP even though it is not an affirmative approval.
cda65fc717ba.proposal: Define and validate a strict verdict schema at the gate boundary. On publish runs, require verdict='ship', a valid bounded numeric score, complete hard-check data, and the expected rubric/version metadata; treat every unknown or malformed value as blocked.
cda65fc717ba.evidence: shared/showrunner_gate.py lines 83-95 append a reason only for the exact string 'block' and for score is None, then return blocked=bool(reasons); no branch requires an explicit 'ship' verdict or rejects unknown verdict values.

df9eeac8ee28.observation: scripts/showrunner_review.py computes a final ship/block verdict from score and auto-fails, while shared/showrunner_gate.py separately interprets that verdict and adds publish-context rules. 6be0849a55e4.title: Cache hits bypass the recent-use penalty
6be0849a55e4.observation: On a cache miss, _prefilter subtracts media_usage.penalty(url) for assets used in the last 14 days. On a cache hit, search() rebuilds Candidate objects from cached dictionaries and returns immediately, so the current usage ledger is never consulted.
6be0849a55e4.proposal: Cache raw candidate facts, then rerun dynamic scoring on every read. Add a regression test that caches a URL, records it as used, and verifies that the next cache hit lowers its rank.
6be0849a55e4.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 1460-1472 apply media_usage.penalty() only inside _prefilter; lines 1572-1587 return cached candidates directly; funnel/media_usage.py lines 49-63 define the live 14-day penalty lookup.

3cca8a711ec4.title: Cached scores are not recomputed
3cca8a711ec4.observation: _cache_put stores Candidate.to_dict(), including the final score after time-dependent freshness, staleness, recent-use, same-host, and LLM adjustments. Cache hits restore that score unchanged for up to 48 hours.
3cca8a711ec4.proposal: Persist only source facts in the cache and recompute derived score components after every read, or store score components separately with explicit timestamps and invalidation rules.
3cca8a711ec4.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 145-154 include score in Candidate.to_dict(); lines 181-193 persist those dictionaries; lines 1475-1513 add dynamic score adjustments; lines 1572-1587 restore and return cached scores; CACHE_TTL_SEC is 48 hours at lines 105-107.

e02d4cf673bd.title: Timed-out providers lack terminal outcomes
e02d4cf673bd.observation: search() stops collecting after a 15-second timeout and calls shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True). Already-running provider calls continue, can still update shared quota state, and have no run-scoped completed, cancelled, or timed-out record.
e02d4cf673bd.proposal: Add a structured provider outcome ledger and per-provider deadline handling so every started provider reaches a recorded terminal state before the search result is finalized, while preserving the overall latency limit.
e02d4cf673bd.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 1596-1632 stop result collection after 15 seconds and use shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True); lines 196-241 update shared quota state from provider calls.

4c58349192b8.title: Asset metadata is assigned by provider class
4c58349192b8.observation: Candidate exposes source_class and license as asset metadata, but _prefilter assigns many values from a provider-name map rather than from item-level fields returned for the selected asset. Some stored values explicitly say verification is still required.
4c58349192b8.proposal: Move to a provenance-first asset manifest that stores source page, creator, original rights text, retrieval time, selection reason, and verification status for each chosen asset. Require item-level evidence for any lane that depends on it.
4c58349192b8.evidence: funnel/media_funnel.py lines 141-148 define source_class and license fields; lines 1420-1458 assign those fields from provider categories and include values such as 'verify per item'.

653acb99b575.title: Third-capture QA passes clips when QA itself crashes
653acb99b575.observation: The full review gate promises NEVER to raise, but its outer exception handler appends 'qa internal error (failed open)' and then sets verdict='pass'. Any unexpected probe, contact-sheet, vision, or local QA failure inside that try block therefore authorizes the clip instead of withholding it.
653acb99b575.proposal: Fail closed on QA-internal errors: return verdict='fail' (or an explicit quarantine/error verdict that every caller treats as non-publishable), preserve the exception text as evidence, and add a regression test that forces an internal QA exception and proves the clip cannot advance.
653acb99b575.evidence: third_capture/clip_qa.py, review(): the docstring says 'QA-internal error fails open'; the outer except appends 'qa internal error (failed open)' and assigns verdict = 'pass'.

75af24a46374.title: Dropping an overlength replay leaves its whoosh cue behind
75af24a46374.observation: build_edl() adds a 'whoosh' SFX cue at the start of an appended replay. If the output exceeds 52 seconds, it removes replay segments but filters cues only where cue[1] != 'riser'. The replay never added a riser, so its whoosh survives after the replay segment is gone and can fire at the old end-of-timeline position.
75af24a46374.proposal: When removing replay segments, remove the cue(s) owned by that replay using the replay start time or explicit cue ownership instead of filtering the unrelated 'riser' label; add a unit test for an over-cap EDL with replay enabled.
75af24a46374.evidence: third_capture/auto_edit.py, build_edl(): the replay branch appends (out_t, 'whoosh'); the subsequent max_out cleanup deletes kind=='replay' segments but removes only cues whose label is 'riser'.

cf263a770061.title: Hard novelty gate treats probe failure as a clean video
cf263a770061.observation: DIRECTOR.md defines NOVELTY as gate 0, says it is enforced rather than advised, and says a stale span rejects the render. novelty_check() obtains duration with ffprobe inside a broad exception handler, but on any exception it returns an empty list. Empty means no stale spans, so a broken/missing probe silently satisfies the hard gate.
cf263a770061.proposal: Represent 'could not evaluate novelty' separately from 'no novelty violations' and make the director fail closed when gate 0 cannot run. Persist the probe failure in the scorecard/report so a tooling outage is distinguishable from a genuinely clean film, with a test that forces ffprobe failure.
cf263a770061.evidence: data_learning/DIRECTOR.md, 'The hardline rule' and scorecard gate 0 require novelty enforcement; scripts/no_dull_beats.py, novelty_check(), catches any duration-probe exception and immediately returns [].

79e94e61b5a9.title: Proof-mode ledger is evidence without an integrity boundary
79e94e61b5a9.observation: capture_cli.py describes itself as the truthfulness layer whose replay and measured claims come from recorded artifacts. It hashes files that callers explicitly record, but the displayed shell_line is accepted directly from the caller, and save_ledger()/load_ledger() simply serialize and deserialize ordinary JSON. Nothing in this module binds argv, terminal events, shell_line, measurements, and referenced file hashes into one identity that a downstream renderer can verify before replay.
79e94e61b5a9.proposal: Evolve proof mode toward a content-addressed proof manifest: derive or validate the displayed command from argv, hash a canonical ledger payload containing argv/events/measurements/artifact hashes, and require downstream composition to verify that identity before treating a capture as proof. Keep human-readable JSON, but make tampering or accidental post-capture edits detectable rather than trusted by convention.
79e94e61b5a9.evidence: third_capture/capture_cli.py: capture() stores shell_line as shell_line or ' '.join(argv); record_file() hashes selected files; save_ledger() writes json.dumps(asdict(cap)); load_ledger() only json.loads() the file with no ledger-integrity verification.

69a886343361.title: Production shortfall test never executes the red exit path
69a886343361.observation: TestRedVersusPaused.test_the_run_still_goes_red_on_any_shortfall says it proves the orchestrator exits non-zero when production is incomplete, but the test only reads scripts/run_trending_daily.py as text and checks for the substrings `if not complete:` and `repair/retry required`. It would still pass if that branch became unreachable, returned zero, or wrote the wrong outcome. The current runtime evidence for 20260808 shows trending ended 1/6 with status repair_required, so this is an actively important contract rather than a theoretical edge.
69a886343361.proposal: Replace or supplement the source-text assertion with an executable regression test around the real completion decision: drive a fixture outcome below expected and assert the orchestrator's callable/CLI result is non-zero and the persisted production outcome remains repair_required. Keep all showrunner and quarantine holds sovereign; the test should verify visibility of the shortfall, not force uploads.
69a886343361.evidence: tests/test_production_outcome.py, TestRedVersusPaused.test_the_run_still_goes_red_on_any_shortfall(), reads scripts/run_trending_daily.py and uses two assertIn() calls instead of executing the branch; doctor/evidence.json dated 20260809 records trending 1/6 for 20260808 with status repair_required.

9b8b29a78b87.title: Malformed production-outcome test cannot detect a regression
9b8b29a78b87.observation: TestTheAlarmReadsTheOutcome.test_a_junk_outcome_file_is_ignored writes `{not json` to the trending outcome file, calls alarm.check(), and then asserts only that the returned object contains an `alarms` key. That key is part of the normal result shape, so the assertion does not establish how malformed outcome state is handled and can stay green across materially different behaviors.
9b8b29a78b87.proposal: Make the test assert the actual safety contract for malformed outcome state: it should be surfaced as a named diagnostic or at minimum be proven unable to masquerade as a production_complete outcome. Assert the specific code/notes/status expected from the chosen stronger behavior rather than the existence of the top-level `alarms` field.
9b8b29a78b87.evidence: tests/test_production_outcome.py, TestTheAlarmReadsTheOutcome.test_a_junk_outcome_file_is_ignored(), writes invalid JSON and finishes with `self.assertIn("alarms", r)`; neighboring tests assert specific alarm codes, showing the malformed case is the outlier.

9943424b8251.title: Workflow policy tests pin text tokens instead of executable behavior
9943424b8251.observation: The production-outcome suite extracts sections of daily.yml with string splits and then checks for fragments such as `exit 1`, `exit 0`, `production_runs`, `uploaded`, and counter messages. These tests protect wording and rough shape, but they do not prove that the YAML remains syntactically valid, that the intended branch conditions bind to the intended steps, or that the shell snippets produce the claimed exit/status behavior.
9943424b8251.proposal: Move the load-bearing pause/counter/completion policy into testable functions or checked scripts and have the workflow call them, then test inputs and exit codes directly. Add a lightweight workflow-structure validation that parses the YAML and verifies step conditions/identifiers, so refactors can change comments and formatting without weakening executable coverage.
9943424b8251.evidence: tests/test_production_outcome.py defines counter_step() and stop_step() by splitting the raw daily.yml text, and TestRedVersusPaused/TestAPausedRunIsNotAGreenRun assert string fragments from those slices; .github/workflows/daily.yml contains the actual preflight, skipped-run, orchestrator, and failure-counter shell logic those tests intend to protect.

74db7c4b3786.title: Production safety is tested as seams, not as one state machine
74db7c4b3786.observation: The suite has good focused tests for alarm codes and separate tests for production-outcome policy, but the current production path is validated as isolated seams: fixture outcome -> alarm behavior in one module, source/YAML text -> expected policy tokens in another. There is no test in these two incident-focused modules that drives one synthetic day through incomplete production, persisted outcome, red disposition, next-day alarm interpretation, and the bounded recovery/hold decision as a single contract.
74db7c4b3786.proposal: Build a small deterministic production-state-machine harness around filesystem fixtures and callable orchestration boundaries. Exercise complete, partial, zero-upload, showrunner-held, auto-paused, retry-success, retry-failure, and malformed-state cases across consecutive synthetic days, asserting that stronger gates stay blocking while operational failures remain visible and recoverable.
74db7c4b3786.evidence: tests/test_production_outcome.py separately tests workflow text and alarm.check() against hand-written outcome files; tests/test_daily_alarm.py separately seeds posted logs/bundles and asserts alarm codes. doctor/evidence.json for 20260809 shows the real multi-step failure shape persisted across production: 20260808 trending uploaded 1/6 and remained repair_required.

a544d37c275e.title: Reddit illustrations ignore narrated beat timing
a544d37c275e.observation: The Reddit renderer drops every shot whose image cannot be resolved, then gives each surviving panel an equal share of the entire post-title narration. It never uses each shot's phrase or word timing, so one surviving image is deliberately stretched across the whole story and multiple surviving images change at arbitrary fractions rather than when their beats are spoken. The current evidence contains exactly this live shape: an August 9 Reddit render held the same garbled sign-holder image from 10.71 seconds through the payoff while the narration advanced through multiple beats.
a544d37c275e.proposal: Build the illustrated track from the package's full ordered shot list and phrase-aligned narration times. Refuse or visibly quarantine a story when the verified panels cannot cover those windows; do not let missing panels collapse the schedule and silently stretch a neighbor across unrelated beats. Add a deterministic renderer test proving each panel begins within its own phrase window and that a one-panel multi-shot package cannot pass as fully illustrated.
a544d37c275e.evidence: make_reddit_story.py lines 67-83 skip unresolved shots and return only surviving panels; lines 86-113 compute `per = duration / len(panels)` and concatenate equal-length clips without reading shot phrases or word timings. doctor/evidence.json showrunner entry `he_made_every_favor_need_his_sign_off__s` at 2026-08-09T09:39:46+00:00 reports the same image at mid1 through payoff, about 35 seconds of dead air.

d64b063a21bd.title: Nonnumeric chart values pass structural validation
d64b063a21bd.observation: Graph structure validation checks only that each values array has the same length as years. It does not require numeric finite values or ordered numeric years, and it catches every exception from chart_race.assess as though the engine were absent. With otherwise valid fields, two series containing string values pass structural_problems with an empty problem list and then reach a renderer that performs numeric division, interpolation, and axis arithmetic.
d64b063a21bd.proposal: Validate that years and every series value are finite real numbers, that years are strictly increasing, and that all series lengths match before invoking the drama gate. Remove the blanket exception path: an unavailable drama engine, invalid data, or any assessment exception must make the package structurally ineligible, with the failed field or engine condition named.
d64b063a21bd.evidence: shared/package_schema.py lines 166-186 validate only years/series counts and value-array lengths, then use `except Exception: pass` around chart_race.assess. engines/chart_race.py lines 297-306 and 444-451 assume numeric maxima, comparisons, subtraction, division, and interpolation. Running structural_problems on a valid-shaped graph whose values are strings `['1','2','3','4']` and `['4','3','2','1']` returns `[]`.

d17724dfb1c0.title: Chart preflight cannot see fixed-axis empty openings
d17724dfb1c0.observation: The pre-render chart gate assesses series count, peak, swing, and lead changes, but the renderer always exposes the full year span from frame one and reserves at least 12 percent of the eventual global maximum on the y-axis. A package can therefore pass the data-drama gate while opening as a tiny lower-left stub in a mostly empty plot or producing too little effective motion. On August 9, two chart races were blocked for mostly empty black openings and another passed preflight but hit 1.7 effective fps; trending finished 1/6 after replacement attempts.
d17724dfb1c0.proposal: Add a deterministic composition/motion preflight before the expensive full render: derive opening occupied-area and expected pixel-travel from the same axis/timeline math, or render a cheap low-resolution sample and run the existing temporal/empty-frame measurements. Reject the package before it consumes a slot when those stronger floors fail, and feed the measured reason into replacement authoring. Keep the final showrunner sovereign as the last check.
d17724dfb1c0.evidence: engines/chart_race.py lines 281-335 define assess using only magnitude/swing/crossovers; lines 546-609 keep a monotonic y camera with `global_max * 0.12` and call `set_xlim(years[0], years[-1])` on every frame. scripts/run_trending_daily.py lines 839-851 uses assess as the only chart preflight. doctor/evidence.json entries at 2026-08-09T09:31:44, 09:32:46, and 09:36:41 record two empty-void chart blocks and one 1.7-effective-fps temporal block.

30d9585ddd32.title: Finished-video QA has two conflicting analysis authorities
30d9585ddd32.observation: The repository maintains two separate ffmpeg analyzers for the same finished-video boundary. engines/render_qa checks black open/tail, freezes, A/V drift, and active area and declares analyzer failure fail-open; shared/video_qa separately checks black/freeze/silence/audio/loudness and its passes function declares analyzer failure fail-closed. Trending calls shared/video_qa but explicitly proceeds when qa_report returns None, while third capture calls engines/render_qa. Thresholds, defect coverage, result schemas, and failure semantics can therefore drift by channel even though both modules claim to be shared finished-render QA.
30d9585ddd32.proposal: Consolidate mechanical measurement into one engine with one typed report covering black intervals, freeze, silence, stream/duration integrity, loudness, and active area. Put channel-specific thresholds in thin policy adapters, and require publish paths to record an explicit analyzed/pass/hold/infrastructure-error disposition. Migrate both trending and third capture with parity fixtures before retiring either implementation; preserve or strengthen every current blocking condition.
30d9585ddd32.evidence: engines/render_qa.py lines 11-23 and 133-226 define its checks and fail-open None contract; shared/video_qa.py lines 1-21 and 87-183 independently define overlapping checks and a fail-closed passes(None) contract. scripts/run_trending_daily.py lines 409-435 returns success when qa_report is None or raises, while third_capture/clip_qa.py lines 419-430 imports engines.render_qa.maybe_check.

6e0d256d4c2f.title: Missing showrunner hard-check answers count as passes
6e0d256d4c2f.observation: The reviewer prompt requires answers for all five hard auto-fails, but the decision code only blocks checks that are present as objects with present=true. Missing checks, a missing present field, or an empty checks object are therefore treated as no failures. A model response with maximum dimension grades and checks={} computes score 100 and verdict ship, even though none of the mandatory hard rules was answered. The shared gate then sees an explicit ship with a bounded numeric score and permits a publish run.
6e0d256d4c2f.proposal: Validate the judge response before scoring. Require dimensions to contain every anchored grade with an in-range integer and checks to contain exactly every AUTOFAIL_CHECKS key with a boolean present plus nonempty evidence. Convert any missing, malformed, or extra schema state into an explicit block (or raise so the publish gate holds fail-closed). Add pure tests for empty checks, one omitted check, missing present, wrong types, and a complete all-false response; do not change any existing blocking threshold.
6e0d256d4c2f.evidence: scripts/showrunner_review.py lines 63-67 declare that the model must answer every hard check; lines 122-132 only collect keys that exist as dicts with truthy present; lines 502-532 prescribe the complete JSON; lines 591-598 pass grades.get('checks', {}) directly to that permissive logic. Running compute_score with each WEIGHTS ceiling and decide_verdict(score, {}) on main returns score=100, verdict='ship'; a junk_imagery object containing evidence but no present also returns ship.

ddfcb2ed4837.title: Punch-up guard loses repeated numeric claims
ddfcb2ed4837.observation: numeric_claims returns a set, so it records only whether a normalized number appears at least once. check then compares set differences. A rewrite can delete one of two distinct sentences carrying the same percentage and year, and the guard reports no dropped claim because one copy remains. That contradicts the module's stated rule that every number in the original must still be present and gives a punch-up a mechanical path to remove a repeated quantitative beat.
ddfcb2ed4837.proposal: Preserve numeric-claim multiplicity with a Counter or ordered occurrence list and compare counts in both directions. Report the token and missing or added occurrence count, while retaining the current normalization and money/percent/year precedence. Add a regression fixture where the original uses 40% and 2025 twice in distinct sentences and the rewrite keeps each only once; the original must ship instead of the rewrite.
ddfcb2ed4837.evidence: shared/punchup_guard.py lines 28-32 define numeric token patterns; lines 83-96 build and return a set; lines 133-140 use set subtraction for dropped and invented claims. On main, check({'script':'SpaceX hit 40% in 2025. SpaceX held 40% in 2025.','shots':[]}, {'script':'SpaceX hit 40% in 2025.','shots':[]}) returns (True, []), and both numeric_claims calls return exactly {'40%', '2025'}.

06e600e3ecaa.title: Daily alarm attributes the latest trending report to historical dates
06e600e3ecaa.observation: daily_alarm.check(date) uses dated logs and production outcomes for most channel evidence, but its slot-fill section reads the single root daily_report.json without verifying that any row belongs to date. The file currently contains only August 12 publish times and 20260812 package paths. Calling check('20260811') nevertheless emits trending_short_after_retries saying 2/6 shipped with four replacements, which are August 12 results; the dated August 11 production outcome in the same alarm correctly says 0/6. This creates a contradictory evidence pack and can send repair work toward the wrong day's packages.
06e600e3ecaa.proposal: Give each trending report an explicit report_date and archive it under a date-keyed path, then make the alarm load only the requested date and reject mixed or missing row dates. As a safe transitional check, derive each row's date from publish_at and package_path, require all rows to agree with the requested date, and emit a dedicated stale_or_wrong_daily_report alarm instead of a slot-fill claim when they do not. Add consecutive-day and backfill tests that prove an August 12 report cannot affect an August 11 alarm.
06e600e3ecaa.evidence: scripts/daily_alarm.py lines 422-434 unconditionally read ROOT/daily_report.json and compute shipped/retried without consulting the date argument. daily_report.json on main contains publish_at values only for 2026-08-12 and package paths under state/trending_packages/20260812; executing daily_alarm.check('20260811') produces trending_short_after_retries detail 'trending shipped 2/6; 4 re-authored replacement(s)', while doctor/evidence.json's dated production_repair_trending for 20260811 says 0/6 uploaded and 10 failed.

8dc00d1eadd0.title: Showrunner memory drops the scene diagnosis needed to detect recurrences
8dc00d1eadd0.observation: review_video returns structured checks, weakest_scene, problems, fixes, temporal measurements, and the judge backend, but append_ledger persists only dimensions, one_line, auto_fails, motion, and identity metadata. The doctor evidence is built from the last 60 ledger records, so the durable history cannot group failures by format, scene, failure_class, repair_goal, package source, or repair attempt. Production is now repeating the same broad failure on consecutive days: August 11 evidence records a Reddit story ending on an unchanged clock still for about 11 seconds, and August 12 daily_report records another Reddit story whose content panel is one alarm-clock still for the full roughly 40-second body. The gate blocks both, but its memory cannot express that the same repair class recurred.
8dc00d1eadd0.proposal: Version the verdict ledger and persist the complete normalized diagnosis needed for learning: format/channel, package path or source, checks, weakest_scene fields, problems/fixes, temporal data, and repair-attempt lineage, plus a deterministic failure fingerprint derived from format + hard-check + failure_class rather than model prose. Have evidence generation aggregate counts and consecutive-day recurrences by fingerprint so authoring and renderer work can prioritize repeated causes. Keep raw verdicts append-only and preserve the current rubric hash/model metadata during migration.
8dc00d1eadd0.evidence: scripts/showrunner_review.py lines 608-615 return checks, temporal, weakest_scene, problems, and fixes, while append_ledger at lines 627-648 omits all but dimensions, one_line, auto_fails, motion, judge/model, and rubric_sha. scripts/doctor.py evidence_pack reads only the last 60 ledger lines. doctor/evidence.json records the August 11 garden-gnome Reddit render holding the same clock still through mid4, mid5 and payoff; daily_report.json on main records the August 12 clock-in story blocked because one alarm-clock still occupied the story half for the entire body.

71d8f01ef635.title: Recovered media checkpoints bypass their contract validator
71d8f01ef635.observation: When response.json omits a request or is absent, Phase B reconstructs pointers with recovered_media and adds them to idx['media']. It then calls validate_response_media on the unchanged response object, not on the augmented index or a rebuilt response. The recovered entries therefore never reach checkpoint_problems, contract matching, deterministic-filename checks, sharing checks, dimension checks, or duplicate-file detection. pointer_from_checkpoint admits any object marked verified that has only request_id, drive.file_id, and image.sha256. Later, the fetch loop reads the unvalidated recovered pointer from idx and can pin it. This is the exact recovery mode made important by the August 12 critical finalizer-no-artifact alarm.
71d8f01ef635.proposal: Validate each checkpoint before converting it, using the requested date, active bundle identity, request id, prompt, and request kind, then validate a single merged response view so recovered and explicit pointers receive identical cross-entry checks. Refuse any recovered entry that fails and send the shot to the existing self-fill path. Replace the current source-order test with a behavioral test that plants a verified-looking checkpoint with the wrong schema, date, bundle, filename, sharing, and dimensions and proves Phase B refuses it.
71d8f01ef635.evidence: scripts/exchange_phase_b.py lines 480-502 add recovered pointers only to idx; lines 529-532 validate response instead; lines 657-681 later fetch and pin from idx. shared/media_checkpoint.py lines 1303-1339 make pointer_from_checkpoint require only status, request_id, file_id, and sha256, while checkpoint_problems at lines 464-530 defines the stronger trust contract. On main, a checkpoint with schema='wrong', date='20200101', bundle.identity='wrong', no folder/sharing/filename/dimensions, but status='verified', file_id and a 64-hex sha produces 13 checkpoint_problems yet recovered_media('20260813') returns it as fulfilled. tests/test_checkpoint_recovery.py only asserts that the recovery call appears textually before validation, so it passes without proving the merged object is what gets validated.

2f7ee366fb9b.title: Malformed DONE payloads count as completed Finalizer runs
2f7ee366fb9b.observation: is_done returns true when DONE exists but is not JSON, and it also returns true for an empty object or an empty date. Phase B consequently enables the stricter DONE branch and satisfies --require-done even though the closure artifact does not prove its production date. A missing or malformed response is logged, but the function continues into recovery, self-fill, and rendering. This contradicts the Finalizer contract that DONE is a separate, verified JSON commit written only after response.json reads back successfully.
2f7ee366fb9b.proposal: Make is_done true only for a JSON object whose date exactly equals the requested YYYYMMDD date; all malformed, non-object, missing-date, and wrong-date shapes must be false with a diagnostic. Add table-driven tests for invalid JSON, arrays, null, {}, empty dates, wrong dates, and the one valid payload. Keep the no-DONE backstop as the explicit recovery path rather than laundering a bad marker into completion.
2f7ee366fb9b.evidence: shared/exchange_bundle.py lines 475-487 explicitly return True on JSON parse failure and accept a blank stamped date. scripts/exchange_phase_b.py lines 452-478 use is_done to decide checkpoint requirements and --require-done. Running is_done('20260813') against DONE contents 'not json', '{}', and '{"date":""}' returns True for all three; only a different nonempty date returns False. tests/test_exchange.py test_done_marker_is_date_scoped covers missing, wrong, and correct dates but has no malformed or empty-payload cases.

44caf5d53209.title: Last-resort topic media bypasses the image URL trust boundary
44caf5d53209.observation: The second self-fill lane calls resolve_entity_media, which runs topic_media.search and accepts only a URL that passes url_is_image. If every candidate fails that verification, the third lane immediately calls topic_media.search again and returns the first nonempty URL without any check. The fallback can therefore select the exact dead, HTML, or non-image candidate the declared trust boundary just rejected, undermining the reason the verifier exists and creating another route to blank or unrelated shot media.
44caf5d53209.proposal: Expose a verified-candidate helper from entity_media or make topic_media return typed candidates with verification state, then have every self-fill lane consume only verified image URLs. Avoid repeating the same source search after a verified resolver has exhausted it. Add a test where topic_media returns one candidate and url_is_image rejects it; self_fill must return None or continue to a genuinely different verified provider, never return the rejected string.
44caf5d53209.evidence: scripts/exchange_phase_b.py lines 276-294 call entity_media.resolve_entity_media and then topic_media.search, returning the latter's first nonempty string. funnel/entity_media.py lines 313-354 wrap topic_media.search and require url_is_image at lines 342-349; lines 363-396 name that function as the trust boundary. funnel/topic_media.py lines 234-280 aggregate URLs without verifying them. With media_funnel.search mocked empty, resolve_entity_media mocked None, and topic_media.search returning ['unverified-candidate'], self_fill returns 'unverified-candidate'.

ab49431193c5.title: The versioned exchange response schema is not enforced
ab49431193c5.observation: The frozen registry contract names chatgpt-exchange-response/v1, and successful August 13 output declares schema, date, status, and contract. No shared validator requires those envelope fields. response_index accepts any dictionary containing media or packages; contract_problems explicitly tolerates a missing contract declaration; and Phase B then hands authored, explainer, curiosity, and punch-up sections to separate consumers with different local checks. A response can therefore omit its schema, date, status, and contract while still changing packages and scripts, even though only its media pointers receive centralized validation.
ab49431193c5.proposal: Define one typed validator for the complete chatgpt-exchange-response/v1 envelope: exact schema and production date, explicit terminal status, required frozen-contract identity, allowed top-level keys, and structural validation for every response section before any consumer mutates state. Introduce it in report-only mode against captured historical responses, update the scheduled-worker contract to emit any newly required fields, then make Phase B refuse invalid sections while preserving valid independent sections and the existing no-response backstop. Retire the intentional silent-contract compatibility case once all live workers emit the current schema.

5ac409690185.title: Third's fallback slate can never meet its registered target
5ac409690185.observation: The registry is the declared authority and requires six Third clips per day, but the live default template says count=4. When there is no authored day directory, run_third reads that template count and synthesizes exactly four packages without consulting the registry. A flawless fallback run therefore tops out at 4/6; any one quality rejection produces the 3/6 shape in the August 13 alarm. The committed Third QA history confirms that production synthesized four slots on August 10 through August 14, including three successes and one rejection on August 13.
5ac409690185.proposal: Derive the synthesized package count from channel_registry.target_count('third') and treat any template count as invalid drift rather than a second authority. Keep story_count as a bounded format allocation inside that registered total. Add a production-level test that removes the dated package directory, resolves the live registry fixture, and proves run_third creates exactly the registered target with unique deterministic slugs; make the workflow fail visibly if the two sources ever disagree.

A direct main-branch read prints registry target 6 and fallback count 4.

ec1665fbf9fa.title: An unrecognized premise-judge response is recorded as a pass
ec1665fbf9fa.observation: premise_ok asks the adversarial brain for a strict PASS or REJECT verdict, but only the literal REJECT branch blocks. Any other parsed object, including {}, a misspelled verdict, or a structurally unrelated JSON object, falls into the else branch and is labeled llm-pass. That turns a malformed answer into affirmative quality evidence even though the prompt says to default to rejection when unsure and the module describes the publish control as fail-closed.
ec1665fbf9fa.proposal: Accept only the exact normalized verdict PASS as approval and exact REJECT as rejection. Treat every missing, unknown, non-string, or malformed verdict as unavailable evidence and retain the deterministic result without labeling it an LLM pass; if the brain is intended to be binding, hold instead. Add table-driven cases for {}, null, arrays, lowercase valid values, unknown tokens, prose around JSON, and both exact verdicts.
ec1665fbf9fa.evidence: scripts/editorial_gate.py lines 138-156 specify an adversarial strict PASS|REJECT response and tell the judge to default to rejection. Lines 157-164 parse any JSON object, block only when verdict uppercases to REJECT, and label every other object llm-pass. There are no premise_ok or pre_render_verdict tests in tests/, scripts/test*, or data_learning/tests/. With shared.script_generator._call_llm mocked to return '{}', premise_ok on a deterministic-floor-passing title/hook returns {'ok': True, 'reasons': [], 'judge': 'llm-pass'}.

9fe73cb62e3f.title: Quality-policy overrides have no schema or safety floor
9fe73cb62e3f.observation: The binding quality policy says malformed overrides are ignored and that autonomous publishing stays off, but load copies recognized config values without type, range, or cross-field validation and lets environment variables override every field. A nonnumeric max_attempts survives the broad parse block and crashes during the later int conversion. More importantly, a config can set development_min_overall and owner_review_min_overall to zero and autonomous_publish to true; decide then advances a zero-score film and marks autonomous publishing allowed when the three required judges merely return pass. The ordering among repair, internal, owner, and advancement thresholds is not checked either.
9fe73cb62e3f.proposal: Define and validate a typed policy schema before use: finite 0-10 score bounds, positive integer attempt limits, nonempty required-judge identities, monotonic score bands, and immutable safety invariants for autonomous publishing and minimum floors. Reject the entire override atomically on any invalid field and emit a durable diagnostic rather than combining partially trusted values. Limit environment overrides to operational tuning explicitly approved by the registry, never safety-bar removal. Add adversarial config and environment tests for wrong types, NaN/infinity, negative limits, inverted bands, empty required judges, and attempts to enable publishing.
9fe73cb62e3f.evidence: data_learning/judge_policy.py lines 69-102 overlay config values directly, parse environment values using the current value's type, and convert max_unresolved_major/max_attempts after the exception guard. Lines 167-245 trust the resulting required_judges, score floors, and autonomous_publish value. A temporary config with judge_policy.max_attempts='abc' raises ValueError from load. A config with development_min_overall=0, owner_review_min_overall=0, and autonomous_publish=true loads unchanged; decide advances an overall_10=0 film with three passing judge objects. scripts/test_judge_policy.py covers normal decisions and environment parsing but has no schema, monotonicity, or immutable-safety tests.

ca6665bd598d.title: Two closed-loop orchestrators have already drifted apart
ca6665bd598d.observation: data_learning.judge_loop.run presents itself as the shared render-judge-repair loop, but no production module calls it; scripts/produce.py implements a separate orchestration path using only its lower-level helpers. The unused loop has already drifted in two consequential ways: it opens the attempt manifest before render_fn, so the manifest hashes the prior or absent artifact, and it records a failed render as a non-required pseudo-judge that judge_policy.decide never sees. Three passing judge stubs therefore make the loop return status=pass even when render_fn returns ok=false. Maintaining two state machines makes fixes and invariants land in one while the other continues to advertise itself as authoritative.
ca6665bd598d.proposal: Converge on one production-used state machine with typed attempt phases and terminal outcomes: open an attempt, render, bind the completed artifact identity, require render success, run required judges, plan repair, and persist the final disposition. Make scripts/produce.py a thin adapter around that engine or explicitly retire judge_loop.run after migrating its useful comparison and escalation behavior. Add contract tests that execute the same failure matrix through every channel adapter and prove render failure, absent artifact identity, required-judge failure, stalled repair, and successful advancement produce identical safe outcomes.
ca6665bd598d.evidence: data_learning/judge_loop.py lines 229-258 call JudgingStore.open_attempt before render_fn, record ok=false under the name render, then pass only the configured judge verdicts into judge_policy.decide; the manifest hash read at line 258 was stamped before rendering. data_learning/judging_store.py lines 85-114 show open_attempt writes mp4_sha256 immediately. Repository search finds no judge_loop.run call under scripts/, data_learning/, third_capture/, or .github/; scripts/produce.py record_judging and produce implement their own attempt, decision, comparison, repair, and loop flow. Running judge_loop.run with render_fn returning {'ok': False, 'detail': 'encode failed'} and taste/technical/factual stubs returning pass yields final status 'pass' with no blockers.

612efa85efcb.title: The early Phase B candidate still hands an unfinished day to Daily
612efa85efcb.observation: The paired UTC schedule intentionally wakes Phase B twice so code can choose the 08:30 Central candidate. In winter, the 13:30 UTC run reaches the job at 07:30 CST; because no phase_b_report exists, the workflow guard allows execution, then exchange_phase_b returns 0 because the finalizer window is still open. The workflow nevertheless executes the commit and handoff steps and concludes success. Daily Shorts listens to every completed Phase B run and gates only on conclusion=success, so that intentional no-op is indistinguishable from a completed deterministic handoff and can start rendering an unfinished day one hour early. The existing DST test proves the Python gate's clock decision but does not assert the cross-workflow consequence of a successful no-op.
612efa85efcb.proposal: Make readiness an explicit workflow outcome rather than infer it from exit code. Have the Phase B step expose a ready/applied output or require the dated phase_b_report with a matching date/schema before the workflow can reach a success state that Daily accepts; represent early and already-applied candidates as a non-rendering terminal outcome that cannot satisfy the downstream trigger. Add a workflow contract test for both DST seasons that follows each scheduled candidate through guard, Phase B outcome, workflow conclusion, and Daily's job condition, proving exactly one render-capable handoff per local date.
612efa85efcb.evidence: .github/workflows/exchange_phase_b.yml lines 50-71 document the two candidates and say the wrong one exits 0; lines 148-159 set guard.skip=false whenever no phase_b_report exists; lines 161-197 run commit and handoff solely from that guard. scripts/exchange_phase_b.py lines 91-97 return ready=false before 08:30 Central and lines 400-406 translate that state to process exit 0. .github/workflows/daily.yml lines 39-43 subscribe to every completed Phase B workflow and lines 64-69 accept any success conclusion. Calling backstop_status at 2026-01-15T13:30:00Z returns ready=false at 07:30 CST, while tests/test_split_worker.py lines 558-579 assert only the clock gate and not downstream handoff suppression.

51e40ccf5e7f.title: Current runbooks still prescribe the removed Phase B schedule
51e40ccf5e7f.observation: The primary repository runbook contradicts itself within fifteen lines: it first gives the current 08:30 Central paired-cron design and explains that 12:45 UTC was unsafe, then its clock summary restores 12:45 UTC and calls that time deliberately late. Link the abbreviated fallback text to the authoritative exchange schedule instead of restating clock arithmetic. Add a lightweight documentation assertion that rejects the retired '12:45 UTC backstop' and ambiguous '06:15 backstop' phrases in active runbooks.

09d56163c745.title: The watchdog can go green without preserving its verdict record
09d56163c745.observation: The watchdog's stated purpose is to produce a durable, timestamped verdict that the alarm can read, but its persistence step converts every ci_commit_state failure into a warning. On a day when all task artifacts are present, judge.rc remains zero, so a checkout race, rejected push, or other commit failure leaves no record and the entire watchdog workflow still concludes green. On a failed-task day the later explicit failure makes Actions red, but the alarm still loses the committed record it is designed to consume.
09d56163c745.proposal: Treat verdict persistence as required output: distinguish a clean no-change from a failed commit, retry safe non-fast-forward races against current main, and fail the job if the expected dated verdict files are not present on the remote after persistence. Add a workflow-level test that forces ci_commit_state to fail with judge.rc=0 and judge.rc=1 and proves both cases remain visible, while a genuine no-change remains successful.

825a41037aae.title: Superseded task contracts remain publishable as current instructions

Its checker still exists, and the document does not name the production contract that superseded it. This leaves two internally complete task protocols discoverable as current; choosing the wrong one produces work the live renderer never consumes.

Move the connectivity-test narrative behind an unmistakable historical banner that links to doctor/PROMPTS sections 4-5 and EXCHANGE_PIPELINE, while retaining its checker only as a named diagnostic fixture until a separate cleanup decision is made.

Repository search finds no reference to CHATGPT_MEDIA_HANDOFF.md outside that file, so it has no superseded banner or inbound path from the current contract.

a833d2f37a5c.title: Managing-editor cadence counts rejected Third clips as posts

c8ca85c0ce21.title: Trending analytics loses the format identity needed to manage its mix

66364106b455.title: Run the existing Third story arm to a real sample before changing the mix
66364106b455.observation: Third already assigns one daily slot to attempt a multi-clip story and safely falls back when no genuine arc exists. 87d632368528.title: Reddit media reaches the renderer without a semantic or text-safety gate
87d632368528.observation: The Reddit renderer treats any decodable shot image as verified: it downloads, crops, and composites the asset without checking that it depicts the narrated phrase or that visible text is legible. The August 16 ledger shows this is not hypothetical. The break-room story was illustrated with an Iraq-war memo, a textile wrapper, and a Bugzilla inbox; the gift-card story ended on a generated sign with nonsense lettering; and a replacement inheritance story used BETRAYAL Scrabble tiles, a commercial book cover, and a gummy-bear mousetrap. All three were correctly blocked by the showrunner, contributing to a 3/6 day after nine attempts.
87d632368528.proposal: Add a pre-render shot-asset gate before composition that evaluates every panel against its shot phrase and rejects text-heavy or OCR-garbled imagery. Persist a per-shot pass/hold reason and send held assets through the existing replacement path; if six verified panels cannot be assembled, hold the candidate rather than spending a full render and vision review. Add fixtures for unrelated archival documents, keyword-literal props, commercial covers, and generated fake lettering. Preserve the current showrunner as the sovereign final gate.

8b6949ab0573.title: Reddit rendering ignores the media hashes already in its packages
8b6949ab0573.observation: ChatGPT-supplied Reddit shots carry media_sha256 and media_bytes beside a mutable Google Drive download URL, but the renderer never reads either field. It hashes the URL only to choose a cache filename, downloads whatever bytes the URL currently serves, and accepts them when Pillow can decode them. The rendered asset is therefore not proven to be the asset Phase B verified, even though the package already contains the exact attestation needed to prove it.
8b6949ab0573.proposal: After downloading a shot image, require its byte length and SHA-256 to match media_bytes and media_sha256 whenever those fields are present, before Pillow conversion. Treat mismatch as an unresolved panel and a candidate hold under the existing media-completeness policy, record expected and actual digests in the audit, and add tests for matching bytes, replaced Drive content, truncated downloads, and legacy non-ChatGPT shots without attestations.
8b6949ab0573.evidence: state/trending_packages/20260816/06_reddit-gift-card-scam-wrong-digit.json includes media_sha256 and media_bytes on shots 2 and 4-7 alongside drive.google.com URLs. make_reddit_story.py lines 71-86 reads only image_url/image and never references either attestation field. make_explainer_stacked.py lines 463-529 hashes the URL for a cache filename and validates only response size/content type/decodability; repository search finds no media_sha256 use in either renderer.

1207ec562569.title: Active gated engines have no adoption deadline
1207ec562569.observation: The engine-honesty test correctly rejects an active ungated engine with no consumer and requires decision dates for experimental engines, but it exempts every gated active engine from both rules. Parallax is active, gated, and consumerless with no decision date; lookmatch has the same state. Both can therefore remain advertised as active production capabilities forever without a production trial, consumer, demotion, or explicit decision.
1207ec562569.proposal: Give every active gated engine an owner, a decision date, and a named production trial or demotion criterion. Extend the honesty test so consumerless gated engines must carry that lifecycle metadata and so an expired decision date fails. Trial parallax and lookmatch on a small renderer fixture set under the existing showrunner and mechanical gates; adopt only with measured parity or improvement, otherwise demote them to experimental/deferred rather than leaving them indefinitely active.
1207ec562569.evidence: engines/__init__.py lines 105-146 declares parallax status=active, gated=true, consumers=[], with no decision_date; lines 220-243 do the same for lookmatch. tests/test_engine_registry_honesty.py lines 84-93 skips all gated active engines when requiring consumers, while lines 128-143 requires decision_date only for status=experimental. `python -m unittest tests.test_engine_registry_honesty -v` passes all 10 tests on current main with both consumerless active entries.

66d90578bc9b.title: Renderer randomness is not reproducible or attributable
66d90578bc9b.observation: The same package is not a reproducible render. Reddit randomly chooses a gameplay file and seek point; explainer randomly chooses gameplay, a motion window, and a seek; the retained text-card renderer does the same. None accepts or records a render seed. A rerun after a showrunner block can therefore change background footage independently of the intended repair, making A/B diagnosis, regression reproduction, and audit comparison ambiguous.
66d90578bc9b.proposal: Define a shared render-context contract carrying a deterministic seed derived from package identity plus an explicit attempt number. Route all renderer choices through a local seeded RNG, record the seed and chosen asset/time ranges in a versioned audit manifest, and let repairs increment the attempt deliberately. Add cross-renderer tests proving identical package+attempt inputs produce identical plans while a new attempt changes only declared stochastic choices.
66d90578bc9b.evidence: make_reddit_story.py lines 212-221 calls module-global random.choice and random.uniform. make_explainer_stacked.py lines 1775-1829 calls random.choice/uniform for gameplay and seek selection. make_text_card.py lines 203-220 calls the same global RNG. None of the three build entry points accepts a seed or RNG, and their audit sidecars do not record one.

f6aa3e1f1c66.title: Test the existing superlative doctrine against the finance-heavy explainer queue
f6aa3e1f1c66.observation: Explainer's doctrine already says to favor science, nature, records, scale, and superlatives and avoid dry finance, yet the active story inventory opens with long runs of home prices, mortgage rates, grocery bills, debt, wages, rent, insurance, and retirement topics. In the latest analytics, the 34 retention-bearing titles containing a clear extreme/superlative cue such as largest, hottest, strongest, deepest, longest, or most have a 50.1% median average-view percentage; the other 97 retention-bearing titles have a 29.1% median. The family is broad and noisy, but the repeated median gap is large enough for a controlled slot-level test, not an immediate wholesale rewrite.
f6aa3e1f1c66.proposal: Keep the registered four-per-day cadence and every quality bar unchanged, but register a 28-day explainer topic experiment: reserve one slot per viable production day for a sourced science/nature/scale/superlative story and compare it with the other data-story slots at the same 72-hour age band. Require at least 25 mature uploads in the treatment; primary metric median average-view percentage, guardrails editorial-block rate, factual-correction rate, and short-slate days. If the gap survives, promote that topic family and prune an equal number of unproduced finance-heavy queue entries; otherwise retain the broad mix.
f6aa3e1f1c66.evidence: data_learning/niche.config.json lines 5-6 states the superlative/science doctrine, while its stories beginning at line 14 include repeated finance topics such as home prices (line 43), mortgage rates (63), grocery bills (205), credit-card debt (248), wages (331), rent (371), insurance (559), and retirement (725). A reproducible grouping of state/analytics_explainer/latest.json videos with numeric average_view_percentage yields n=34 and median=50.1 for titles matching largest|hottest|strongest|deadliest|oldest|loudest|longest|driest|fastest|deepest|biggest|most, versus n=97 and median=29.1 for the remainder. config/channel_registry.json lines 221-248 fixes cadence at four and identifies niche.config as the queue authority; retro/20260816/brief.json says Explainer's 72-hour cohort is too thin for a one-day call, which is why this proposal requires a prospective mature sample.
